wy_holdout.blurb: Holdout is a boxy granite formation at Vedauwoo, the crack-climbing hub in the hills between Laramie and Cheyenne, tucked between two better-known zones at roughly 8,250 feet. It is mostly a trad crag, with a couple of sport lines, a few top-rope setups and three boulder problems, some of the trad lines running two pitches. The bulk of the free climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with a solid handful in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, plus one easy and a couple of very hard boulder problems. Expect cracks, offwidths and diagonal seams rather than face holds. The southeast side catches plenty of sun, while the northwest side picks it up late in the day.

wy_baldwin_creek.blurb: Baldwin Creek is a steep dolomite cliff roughly fifteen miles west of Lander, up in the forested hills above the valley. It is a sport-only crag aimed at strong climbers: of 29 bolted lines, around half sit at 5.12, another third at 5.13, and a few reach 5.14, with only a small number of 5.10s and 5.11s to warm up on. The rock is uniform and fine-grained with few cracks, so climbing is sustained and demanding from the ground up. The wall faces south and has little shade, so it can be punishingly hot even on cool autumn days. The drive and walk in are rough, which keeps crowds thin.
wy_baldwin_creek.parking_note: Drive west out of Lander and continue past the end of the pavement on the dirt road up the hill. A 4x4 or high-clearance vehicle is advised for the last stretch. Parking is an undeveloped pull-off beside the road.
wy_baldwin_creek.approach: A faint trail leaves the parking area and runs through conifer forest to the canyon rim, then drops steeply through a gap to the cliff. Fallen trees can hide the path.

wy_beehive_buttress.blurb: Beehive Buttress is the odd one out at Vedauwoo: a bolted granite face in a quiet valley rather than the jam-crack territory the area is known for. Of its 29 routes, nearly all are sport, with a single trad line. Grades run from easy fifth class up to the low 5.12s, but the heart of the crag is 5.10, with a good batch of 5.6 to 5.9 routes for newer leaders. The holds are friendlier than elsewhere in the area, with jugs, slopers and edges, and the rock feels closer to Boulder Canyon than to the sharp slabs nearby. Crowds are far lighter than at the main formations.
wy_beehive_buttress.parking_note: From the Lincoln Monument, take Blair-Wallis Road toward the central area, turn left onto 705J, then left onto 705JA and drive until it becomes too narrow. Both spur roads are rough and unsigned.
wy_beehive_buttress.approach: From where the road ends, follow the old ATV track to the base of the wall.

wy_3_the_roof_area.blurb: The Roof Area is the westernmost and most actively developed sector of Fairfield West, on Fairfield Hill in Sinks Canyon near Lander, at close to 7,900 feet. All 29 routes are bolted, and the sector is named for the huge roof that the trail runs beneath. The dolomite here has a strong reputation for quality. Grades start with a lone easy line and run up to the low 5.13s, with the weight in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so it suits climbers who want steep, pumpy sport climbing instead of a place to learn. Several of the most popular lines earn three or four stars.

wy_lower_remuda.blurb: Lower Remuda is a sport sector on the back side of Wild Iris, the pocketed white dolomite crag on Limestone Mountain southwest of Lander at about 8,600 feet. It holds 29 bolted routes, concentrated in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a few 5.10s, a small number of 5.13s and only a couple of easier lines. Because it sits away from the front of the cliff, it loses the sun in the afternoon, which makes it a useful alternative when the main walls are baking. Climbs are generally short and can be sharp on the fingers, and belay spots are shaded by aspen.

wy_hightower.blurb: Hightower sits at the low, southwestern end of the Southwest Ridge on Reese Mountain, in the Laramie Range of east-central Wyoming, around 6,500 feet. It is a mix of trad and bolted lines, with more trad than sport among its 29 routes. Most of the climbing is 5.10 to 5.11, with a few at 5.12 and a handful of easier climbs. Expect technical, sustained movement on sidepulls, edges and pinches, with steeper climbing on an overhanging upper tier. Reaching it takes a hike up the drainage to the corner of the ridge, so it sees fewer visitors than roadside crags.

wy_the_tunnel_wall.blurb: The Tunnel Wall belongs to the Island area, out at Shoshone Canyon's western end near Cody. The face runs back toward the rear of the Island and rises nearly 200 feet, though most routes are single pitches of about 40 to 90 feet, with one long bolted line near the top. Climbs are mostly sport, spread from the 5.8 range through the 5.12s, and the middle grades of 5.10 and 5.11 are best represented. It faces north and sees only a little early sun, making it a summer choice. The car is only a short stroll from the base.
